# ECN-2026-013 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

## Reason for change
Background: Recent preventive maintenance and operational trend analysis for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 identified recurring coil overheating events and intermittent flow alarms that correlate with reduced cooling performance. Root cause analysis determined that coil thermal stress and marginal cooling capacity at low flow conditions increase the risk of coil insulation breakdown and downstream components being exposed to elevated temperatures. Risk assessment concluded that a formal change to the minimum allowable coil cooling water flow specification and associated verification steps is required to maintain safe operation and prolong coil life.

Change objective: Update the minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and implement revised procedural controls, verification, and records to ensure continued compliance and risk mitigation.

Mandatory value update: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min.

Rationale: Establishing a clearly documented minimum flow value reduces false negatives in alarm interpretation, aligns operator actions with actual equipment capability, and informs maintenance acceptance criteria following component replacement or system restoration.

Related documents: MM-P2-L1-IH02, SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-03

## Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is directly affected by the updated minimum coil cooling water flow requirement and related verification steps.
- Procedures: SOP-P2-L1-03 will be revised to include the updated minimum flow value and step-by-step verification requirements for pre-start checks, start-up, and emergency restart after a cooling system intervention.
- Maintenance plan: MM-P2-L1-IH02 will be updated to include acceptance criteria for cooling system servicing, including component handover checklists that reference the updated minimum flow.
- Safety bulletin: SB-1001 will be referenced in operator briefings to highlight the operational risk mitigations and emergency response implications tied to the cooling flow minimum.
- Training: Operations and maintenance training materials and competency checklists will be updated to reflect the value and associated verification actions.

## Implementation
Scope: The change applies to all activities that affect the cooling circuit, coil assembly, flow measurement devices, and control logic related to EQ-P2-L1-IH02 on line P2-L1.

Actions:
- Update SOP-P2-L1-03 to include the mandatory minimum cooling flow value and explicit acceptance criteria for pre-operational checks. The SOP will require operators to verify that measured flow meets or exceeds the specified minimum before generating a billet heat cycle.
- Update MM-P2-L1-IH02 to add post-service verification steps where maintenance personnel confirm that flow instrumentation is calibrated and that measured flow meets the minimum before returning the heater to service.
- Revise control system alarm setpoints and interlocks to align with the minimum flow requirement. Document the rationale for each setpoint change in local control system change records, and reference SB-1001 for temporary bypass procedures and required authorization when alarms inhibit production.
- Implement a verification checklist to be completed and signed by qualified personnel after any cooling system intervention. The checklist will be retained with equipment maintenance records and referenced in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Conduct a focused training session for operations and maintenance on the updated requirement, its implications, and the new verification checklist. Training attendance and assessment results will be recorded and filed with personnel training records.
- Initiate an initial compliance audit after implementation to confirm that SOP, maintenance documentation, control logic, and training updates are in place and that field verification demonstrates the cooling flow meets the specified minimum during representative operating conditions.

Examples of application:
- Pre-start sequence: Operators will consult SOP-P2-L1-03, perform the flow verification, and sign the pre-start checklist before energizing the heater. If measured flow is below the minimum, the operator will follow the escalation path defined in SB-1001.
- Post-maintenance handover: Maintenance will use the updated MM-P2-L1-IH02 acceptance checklist, demonstrate that flow instrumentation is within calibration and that measured flow meets the minimum, and annotate the maintenance record prior to releasing EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to operations.

Records to keep:
- Revised SOP-P2-L1-03 version and change log entry.
- Updated MM-P2-L1-IH02 maintenance procedure and service acceptance checklists.
- Completed verification checklists associated with any cooling system work on EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Training attendance rosters and competency assessments for personnel who received the update.
- Control system change records and alarm setpoint rationales that reference SB-1001 where applicable.
- Initial compliance audit report and any corrective action records generated from the audit.

Retention and storage: All records listed above will be stored in the document control system and equipment maintenance folder for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Records will be referenced during routine audits and when investigating future cooling-related incidents.

## Approvals
Approval matrix: The engineering change requires documented approval by the responsible equipment engineer, maintenance manager, operations manager for line P2-L1, and safety/compliance representative.

Sign-off deliverables:
- Engineering approval of the revised minimum cooling flow value and supporting technical justification.
- Maintenance approval of MM-P2-L1-IH02 updates and acceptance checklist.
- Operations approval of SOP-P2-L1-03 updates and training plan.
- Safety approval referencing SB-1001 for emergency procedures and temporary bypass authorization.

Post-approval actions:
- Release the revised SOP-P2-L1-03 and MM-P2-L1-IH02 documents through the document control system.
- Schedule and complete training for affected personnel.
- Implement control system changes and complete verification checks documented in the records to keep.

Related documents for reference: MM-P2-L1-IH02, SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-03

Notes: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Compliance with this requirement is mandatory and will be enforced through procedural checks, maintenance acceptance criteria, and control system interlocks.
